context_length: Embedded whole up to 2,644 residues here; longer sequences failed and are left out of every run
summary: The open 1.4B-parameter ESM3; a multimodal generative model over sequence, structure, and function. Here it is used purely as a sequence encoder (1536-dim per-residue embeddings).
architecture: Multimodal transformer that jointly tokenizes sequence, 3D structure, and function into discrete tracks; the smallest 'open' variant. This benchmark consumes only its per-residue sequence-track representations (1536-dim).
pretraining_data: ≈2.78B natural proteins (≈3.15B with synthetic augmentation; 236M structures and 539M function-annotated proteins), ≈771B tokens.
pretraining_objective: Masked generative modeling across the sequence, structure, and function tracks.
key_innovations: First natively multimodal, generative ESM (sequence + structure + function)
Demonstrated de novo design (esmGFP), an order of magnitude larger training than ESM-2
when_to_use: When structure/function-aware pretraining might benefit a property, or to compare a generative multimodal model against masked encoders; while still using single-sequence embeddings.
caveats: Designed as a generative multimodal model; using it only as an embedding encoder ignores its structure/function inputs. Heavier tokenization pipeline than plain PLMs. In this benchmark ESM3 could not embed the 620 sequences of 2,645 residues or more; they are left out of every run, for every model.

citations.title: Simulating 500 million years of evolution with a language model (ESM3)
